segments.expected: Then, because she held them there and did not lean, the other thing came.

segments.expected: It was slow. It was slower than the bollard on the quay. It came and went in long lifts, irregular, a long one and a short one and a long one. That was the flood, she thought, the surges, the thing that Jude had stood at the rail and counted and called every count at once. And under it, so faint that she was not sure, there was something else. Four and four.

segments.expected: He had asked what ash was for of everybody since the autumn. He had asked it of a Marshal on a moor and a foreman on a scarp and his own four on a shed step, and he had been given a hand and a floor and a cell. He had never sounded like this, asking. He sounded as though he had found the answer and did not know yet what it would cost him.

segments.expected: "It's shut," said Penhale. "I felt it from here."

segments.expected: "Ebb," said Penhale. "Twelve fourteen. Out of the boat, officer, if you please. It'll work the ebb now till dawn." He took his hands off the first line. "Three purses shut. On this coast a shut purse is a sealed bag, miss. We tie them at the low water for the Board's sake." He looked sideways at Kiva. "You may talk now, if you've a mind to. I've been talking for both of us."

segments.expected: He was not looking at her heel. He was looking past her, past the post, at the sea side, where the skin lay in the mud. Its far edge had lifted. It was coming up out of the mud in a long grey lip, streaming, as the third skin had come up out of the water at midnight. It was turning over toward the purse, toward Penhale standing in the mud with nobody watching for him.
